subject: Pricing qualification: context length & token volume profiling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: pricing qualification & context-length profiling

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the Acme.ai team. Quick recap + a couple asks so we can put together a tight pricing/rollout recommendation.

Recap (very high level)
- Primary use case: customer-facing summarization + assisted authoring across technical documents and proposals.
- Requirements called out: low latency for interactive flows, some long-context jobs for large documents, and multi-tenant data isolation.
- Target timeline: pilot in Q2, production rollouts in H2 if pilot meets latency & unit cost targets.

Items we need to size pricing properly
1) Token volume: rough monthly forecast (range ok) — monthly total tokens and any seasonality.
2) Prompt / completion profile: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, 50/90/95 percentile completion lengths.
3) Context-length needs: percent of requests that require >8k, >32k, >128k context; example workflows that hit long context.
4) Target budget sensitivity: target $/1M tokens (or target monthly spend) so we can produce options (8k vs 32k vs 128k variants).
5) Any compliance/retention needs (SOC2, VPC/on-prem) that will affect pricing.

I attached a simple token-profiling CSV template — if you can dump sample logs or give rough numbers we can model unit economics quickly.

Next steps
- If you can reply with the items above, I’ll loop in Jordan for pricing scenarios and Dev for the technical implications. We can then propose a pilot configuration (model variant, caching/batching suggestions, and an estimated $/1M token rate given volume).

Thanks — talk soon.

Cheers,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Attached is a quick export (acme-token-profiles.csv) from our prod logs for the past 30 days; numbers are anonymized but representative. High level from our side:

- Monthly token forecast: ~300M tokens (conservative) — can scale to 800M if pilot results look good.
- Avg prompt tokens: ~450 tokens (includes system + user + metadata).
- Avg completion tokens: ~1,200 tokens.
- Percentiles for completion length: 50% ~600, 90% ~2,400, 95% ~5,000.
- Context needs: ~70% of requests are short (fit in 8k), ~25% need up to 32k, ~5% are extremely long (100k+ docs) but we currently chunk them client-side; we could see up to 10% hitting >32k if we switch to single-pass summary jobs.
- Procurement note: target budget for vendor pricing is roughly $1,400 per 1M tokens for our preferred economics in a multi-month committed pilot. Lower if we can get committed annual volume.

Compliance: SOC2 required, customer data isolation preferred but can start on hosted model with strong contract terms.

Let me know if you need sample payloads instead of logs — happy to share.

—Alex

Alex — this is perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround and the CSV. A few quick notes from our side based on the numbers you shared:

- Volume looks great — 300M/mo gives us a good base to propose discounted committed tiers.
- Prompt/completion profile (450 / 1,200) and the 95th at ~5k is consistent with a mix of short interactive + long-form jobs.
- Context split (70% 8k, 25% up to 32k, 5–10% >32k) is helpful. For modeling we’ll assume the conservative 10% long-tail.

Preliminary pricing implications (very rough)
- 8k-optimized variants: best for the 70% short traffic — lowest unit cost; good for interactive latency-sensitive flows.
- 32k variants: typically 1.5x–2.5x per-token cost relative to an 8k-optimized runtime depending on model & infra; appropriate for the 25% mid-length requests.
- 128k or single-pass 100k+: material cost increases and operational considerations (KV cache, memory footprint). For the initial pilot we recommend a hybrid approach: primarily 8k with a routed pool (32k) for mid-length jobs and client-side chunking for the very long docs unless single-pass is a hard requirement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jordan and I will run a unit-economics model for 300M/mo with the 10% long-tail assumption and produce three pricing scenarios (pure hosted, committed discount, and dedicated pilot).
2) Dev — can you flag any implementation caveats for a hybrid rollout and note what sample payloads you’d need to validate latency vs cost?
3) Alex/Priya — if procurement has a target date, let us know so we can align the committed discount proposal.

I’ll attach our baseline pricing vs context doc for reference. Chat soon.

Best,

Thanks for the data, Alex — quick technical callouts from the SE perspective:

- Hybrid routing: We can set up routing policies so short interactive requests hit 8k-optimized pools (lowest latency/cost). Jobs tagged as "document-summarization" can route to 32k pools. This keeps per-request cost down while preserving single-pass accuracy where needed.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching is effective for repeated system prompts or boilerplate; that can reduce effective prompt tokens significantly for interactive flows.
- Batching and quantization: batching strategies and lower-precision kernels reduce per-token GPU cost; we can quantify expected savings once we have the sample payloads.
- 128k single-pass: requires careful kernel memory planning and may push you into dedicated hardware (higher baseline cost). If single-pass >100k is only 5–10%, chunking + stitching often gives >90% of the UX at much lower cost.

For profiling, sample payloads we need:
- 50 sample requests each for short, mid, and long flows (with metadata) — include the full tokenized prompt + expected ground-truth completion length.
- A representative set of large documents (5–10) you’d want single-pass summarized.

If you can drop those into the Drive link Marissa shared (or send a secure link), I’ll run them through our runtime profiler and return latency/cost estimates per 1M tokens.

—Dev
